context.question: Does choosing draft length adaptively improve end-to-end tokens/sec over a tuned fixed gamma for exact T-7 chat decoding?
context.decision: Keep a tuned fixed gamma as default; deeply read P2 and P4 before investing in adaptive-policy development. A bounded diagnostic is conditional on an exactness argument and complete matched timing.
context.target_setting: T-7 chat, batch 1, identical single-GPU resources across arms, exact output-distribution preservation. Closest supplied setting: D-1, CHAT-500, G-A. Actual drafter/GPU and traffic equivalence are unconfirmed.
context.bounds: Offline, explicitly fictional supplied corpus only: ../../../evals/fixtures/speculative-decoding.md. All primary access is excerpt or abstract; no full papers or external retrieval. No exactness proof is supplied. P1/P2 are one versioned result history; P3 is a separate but dependent Kappa/code/CHAT-500 result; P4 is a separately conducted Sigma result using a v1 policy description. P5 adds no experiment; P6 is analogy; P7 empirical provenance is unknown. Three inspected empirical result families do not establish three independent contributions.
context.stop_reason: All seven supplied records inspected. Missing branches: full exactness proofs and implementations, independent target-chat replication, broader hardware/traffic transfer, and P7 methods/results. No live saturation claim.

claims.statement: The original timing reports adaptive gamma improving tokens/sec by 9% over best fixed gamma in T-7 chat; this observation is superseded by C2.
claims.scope: T-7, D-1, CHAT-500, batch 1, G-A; best fixed gamma=4 chosen on the same evaluation set

evidence.locator: local:P1-v1, Table 3; Section 6; corrected by local:P2-v2 errata
evidence.observation: +9% relative tokens/sec, mean over 3 seeds, no interval. Forecasting head adds 3% latency and is included, but P2 identifies omitted adaptive-arm draft KV-cache rebuild time. Prompt count and uncertainty construction unreported.
evidence.analyst_inference: Historical result only; do not count as current direct support or as an independent result alongside v2.

assessment.reason: Primary excerpt supports the historical report; inspected errata explicitly replace its timing result.
assessment.limitation: Asymmetric timing invalidates use of the reported 9% as an all-in current gain; test-set comparator selection also remains.

uses.decision: Reject the original 9% as current investment evidence
uses.transfer_assumption: None; retained solely as superseded history

claims.statement: Corrected adaptive-versus-fixed timing gives +2% relative tokens/sec with a 95% interval of [-3%, +7%], leaving useful target-setting improvement unresolved.
claims.scope: T-7, D-1, CHAT-500, batch 1, G-A; all other settings as P1, including fixed gamma selected on the same evaluation set

evidence.observation: +2% relative tokens/sec; 95% interval [-3%, +7%]; 5 seeds; cache rebuild timing fixed. Interval construction, prompt count, actual hardware memory/residency and exactness argument unreported.
evidence.analyst_inference: Closest supplied evidence to target chat. Both modest loss and gain remain compatible with the reported interval; it establishes neither zero benefit nor reliable superiority.

assessment.reason: Corrected primary result excerpt inspected; support is for the scoped estimate and its uncertainty, not a positive-effect conclusion.
assessment.limitation: One dataset/drafter/GPU type; test-set fixed-gamma selection; no supplied correctness proof or detailed interval method.

uses.decision: Keep fixed gamma as default and prioritize corrected paper for a deep read
uses.transfer_assumption: CHAT-500/D-1/G-A must represent intended traffic and resources; exactness remains a separate gate

claims.statement: Adaptive gamma improves tokens/sec by 11%, with a 95% interval of [6%, 16%], on the reported T-9/G-B chat setup.

evidence.analyst_inference: Positive within reported scope, but transfer to smaller T-7/G-A is untested. Shared code makes the C8 timing defect a possible inherited threat, not a confirmed P3 defect; this is not independent replication of P2.

assessment.reason: Primary main result excerpt inspected; no inference that its interval applies to T-7.
assessment.limitation: Model/GPU mismatch and dependence on Kappa code/data; correction provenance unknown. A separate family label does not establish independence.
